subject: Recap & benchmark plan: Redwood vs hyperscalers (latency focus)
messages:
From: Lina Santos <lina.santos@dataforge.ai>

Cc: Victor Park <victor.park@dataforge.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — quick recap and request for latency-focused comparisons

Hi Grace / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — Victor and I appreciated seeing Redwood's runtime and the live generation flows. A couple of quick items we agreed on during the call and a formal request so we can move to a fast evaluation: 

- Goal: quantify p95/p99 latency and sustained tokens/sec for our primary chat workload and a batched embedding pipeline. We need numbers that reflect realistic client traffic (burstiness + warm KV-cache).
- Baseline: we want Redwood vs our current hyperscaler-managed endpoints (HyperscalerX and HyperscalerY). We'll provide sample traces and token distributions.
- Constraints: must use the same model family and comparable quantization profiles where possible; we care about cold-start behavior for scaling, and steady-state p95/p99 at 100–500 concurrent requests.

Deliverables we'd like from Redwood: proposed A/B test plan, exact measurement harness (endpoints, scripts), a p95/p99 table for short/medium/long contexts (32/128/512 tokens), tokens/sec (sustained), and notes on caching/batching settings used. Can you confirm feasibility and an estimated timeline (we're hoping for a one-week sprint)?

Attachments: dataforge-demo-slides.pdf (slides from today's call)

Best,
Lina
Senior ML Platform Engineer
DataForge

Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap and request for latency-focused comparisons

Lina — great to hear, and thanks for the clear ask. We can run a latency-focused sprint and provide the A/B results you outlined. High level plan below; I put owners and target dates.

Plan (one-week sprint attempt):
- Day 0 (today): confirm model/config details and get sample traces from you (owner: Lina).
- Day 1–2: Redwood engineers stand up test harness against your payloads & Hyperscaler endpoints (owner: Rishi).
- Day 3: run controlled A/B runs (cold-start + steady-state) for seq lengths 32 / 128 / 512; concurrency windows at 50 / 200 / 500 (owner: Rishi).
- Day 4: analyze p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec; flag differences due to batching/quantization. Produce short deck.
- Day 5: sync, handoff results and next-recommendations; decision point on production pilot.

Measurement details we'll use unless you prefer alternatives: 30-minute steady-state windows, warm-up of 10 minutes to populate KV caches, synthetic traffic shaped from your traces (burst factor 3), and both single-region and cross-region checks. We'll report p50/p95/p99 (95th/99th percentiles) and sustained tokens/sec measured at the model output.

I'll track action items in the test plan and share the link. If that schedule looks tight on your side, we can stretch to 10 business days.

Action items:
- Lina: share sample traces + model/version constraints by EOD Thu (4 Nov).
- Rishi: prep harness and test config by Fri (6 Nov).
- Aditya: confirm procurement/contract path if we need dedicated capacity for the test.

Thanks — I'll attach a short sprint plan to follow.

—
Grace O'Connor

Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap and request for latency-focused comparisons

Thanks — extra technical detail from my side to ensure apples-to-apples: 

Test harness / measurement specifics I propose:
- Models: run the same model family (we'll aim for an LLaMA-variant you already use); where Hyperscalers only expose float16 endpoints we'll try to match Redwood's float16 path and a quantized-int8 path if you want cost comparisons.
- Sequence lengths: 32 / 128 / 512 tokens; measure both request-latency (end-to-end) and internal token-throughput (tokens/sec).
- Warm/cold: define cold as an idle node that triggers a new container/pod; cold-start windows: 10 cold starts per endpoint spread across run. Warmed runs: a 10 min warm-up and 30 min measurement window.
- Concurrency: synthetic clients at 50 / 200 / 500 concurrency with Poisson arrivals to simulate burstiness.
- Caching: ensure Redwood's KV cache warm-start (reuse between requests) vs Hyperscaler behavior; we will toggle prefix caching on/off to isolate its effect.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 (latency in ms), 95% CI on tokens/sec, error-rate (5xx), tail jitter (stddev p99).
- Environment: single-region US-West 2; if DataForge wants cross-region, we'll add a single cross-region check for p99 delta.

Notes on expected differentiators: Redwood's continuous batching + KV-cache tends to reduce tokens/sec variance and tail latency when prefix-cache hit-rate is >40%. Hyperscalers often exhibit higher cold-start p99 due to heavier platform plumbing; we'll capture that. Quantization differences (int8) will usually improve tokens/sec but can slightly shift p99; we'll call that out.

I'll own the harness. Can you provide the sample traces and the exact model name + tokenizer configs? Also, any hard SLOs you have (e.g., p99 < 500 ms) will help prioritize settings.

- Rishi
Principal ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
